text: Chapter 8 / 19 von Neumann Fourier stability analysis Learning goal: Examine amplification by wavenumber, primarily for constant coefficients on a uniform grid with periodic or infinite domains. Insert a periodic sinusoidal wave and examine how the difference scheme changes its amplitude and phase. A linear, constant-coefficient scheme on a uniform grid can be decomposed into Fourier modes. This is von Neumann analysis. Neumann is a person's name here. This analysis is not the procedure for imposing the normal-derivative Neumann boundary condition introduced later. Boundary treatments on finite domains require checks beyond the interior Fourier analysis. Substitute a single mode Insert a complex grid mode exp(i jθ) into the difference equation. Linearity and constant coefficients preserve its shape at the next time, multiplied by a complex number G. Real waves can be represented using the real and imaginary parts. Here i is the imaginary unit satisfying i²=-1, and exp(i jθ)=cos(jθ)+i sin(jθ). Complex notation handles sine and cosine together. Upwind and Lax-Wendroff schemes Consider advection with speed a>0 and Courant number ν=aΔt/h. For a continuous wavenumber k, θ=kh. Examine the full range representable by the grid, not just low wavenumbers. The roles of magnitude and argument For a scalar periodic problem, |G|≤1 for every mode ensures that discrete L2 does not grow. This is a useful sufficient condition. Lax-type uniform stability can also allow bounds such as 1+CΔt; a value of |G| slightly greater than 1 alone is not a universal instability test. The argument describes phase error, examined in Chapter 11. A small worked example The code checks both the analytic G and the result of advancing a complex Fourier array by one step of the actual difference update. These provide separate paths for checking the derived formula and implementation signs. For FTCS with Courant number 0.6, θ=π/2 gives |G|=√(1+0.6²)>1. This fixed factor is raised to an increasing number of steps, destroying uniform stability at fixed physical time. from cmath import exp from math import pi nu, theta = 0.6, pi/2 g_up = 1-nu+nu*exp(-1j*theta) print(abs(g_up), g_up.real, g_up.imag) symbols.csv contains amplitude, phase, and group-speed data by wavenumber. The implemented mode update must agree with the analytic formula within the fixed absolute bound 1e -12. Figure 8: One-step amplitude multipliers at Courant number 0.6. Two stable methods and the intentionally unstable FTCS control are compared at the same wavenumbers. Show answer No. Short grid-wavelength modes may be unstable. Question 2: With finite-domain boundaries, is the interior |G| generally sufficient? Show answer No. Also examine a matrix or energy estimate including the boundaries, and actual boundary-condition examples. Common pitfalls Do not extend this analysis unconditionally to variable coefficients, nonlinear equations, or nonuniform grids. For multiple components or nonnormal systems, consider more than eigenvalues. Key points Substitute the mode into the actual difference equation. Read amplitude and phase separately.
